item.title: Sistemi Operativi
item.description:
Abstract

Obiettivo dell’insegnamento è quello di fornire i concetti fondamentali che sono alla base dei moderni sistemi operativi, con particolare enfasi sulla gestione della concorrenza, della memoria e del file system. Ogni concetto sarà trattato dal punto di vista teorico. Per i concetti più importanti, la trattazione riguarderà anche aspetti più pratici, in modo da familiarizzare con la loro complessità realizzativa.

item.title: Network Security
item.description:
Abstract

The course aims to present and make students understand the technological, infrastructural, and in part, also economic issues related to computer network security. The course covers both the defensive and attacking aspects of network security. The course also covers a practical part, to allow students to immediately apply some of the acquired knowledge. The practical part also covers soft skills as well at the ability to communicate and present technical work to peers.

item.title: Ethical Hacking
item.description:
Abstract

The aim of the teaching is for students to experience the most common techniques and strategies used to build computer attacks, detect them, and analyze their behavior with the final goal of learning how to prevent or mitigate such attacks. A further aim of the course is to develop skills in communicating and presenting one’s work to colleagues.

item.title: CyberChallenge.IT
item.description:
Capture the Flag activity at UniTN

We participate in the CyberChallenge.IT programme 2027; registrations open in December. We run a training programme for a selected number of students.

Lectures take place in DISI rooms. Students admitted to the programme receive an email with further details; additional information is available on the UniTN venue page .

item.title: MITRE's eCTF
item.description:
Embedded security, in practice

The Embedded Capture the Flag (eCTF) is MITRE’s attack-and-defend competition for secure embedded systems. Teams design and implement a system against a shared set of requirements, then analyse and attack the other teams’ designs.

item.title: AgentLSD: Evaluating AI Security Agents Under Adversarial Task Contamination
UniTN at CCS 2026 and AISec 2026
item.description: Matteo Golinelli and Carlo Ramponi will travel to The Hague to present two accepted papers at ACM CCS 2026 and its colocated AISec workshop. Carlo will present Mitigating Code Injection Attacks on Modern GPUs , while Matteo will present AgentLSD: Evaluating AI Security Agents Under Adversarial Task Contamination .
